s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic progressive vascular skin lesions with neurological and familial components
salient_findings: Bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
key_facts: Female patient in her early 50s
Multiple skin lesions on the lower legs
Lesions have been growing slowly since age 24
Lesions bleed occasionally after trauma
Patient uses a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia
History of intracranial hemorrhage
Recurrent seizures at age 4
Lipolymphedema of the lower legs due to functional venous insufficiency
Family history of similar conditions
Father died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography showed intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations
Histopathology revealed dilated venous-like malformations with thrombosis
Genetic testing detected a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

shortlist.label: Cerebral cavernous malformations
shortlist.why_kept: KRIT1 variant detected, matches family history of intracranial hemorrhage and patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Osler-Weber-Rendu syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Hereditary condition with vascular malformations, matches patient's skin lesions and family history

shortlist.label: Capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Matches patient's skin lesions and presence of vascular malformations

shortlist.label: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
shortlist.why_kept: Hereditary condition with vascular malformations, matches patient's skin lesions and family history of bleeding

shortlist.label: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Matches patient's skin lesions, lipolymphedema, and presence of vascular malformations

raw.rationale: The patient's history of intracranial hemorrhage, right-sided hemiparesis, and hemianopsia, combined with the detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, strongly supports this diagnosis. KRIT1 mutations are commonly associated with cerebral cavernous malformations.

rejected.label: Osler-Weber-Rendu syndrome
rejected.why: While this condition involves vascular malformations, the presence of a KRIT1 variant and the specific combination of symptoms and family history better align with cerebral cavernous malformations.

rejected.label: Capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically involves different types of vascular malformations and is not as strongly associated with KRIT1 mutations or the patient's specific symptoms.

rejected.label: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by telangiectasias and arteriovenous malformations, but the patient's symptoms and genetic findings are more consistent with cerebral cavernous malformations.

rejected.label: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
rejected.why: This condition involves port-wine stains, varicose veins, and bony and soft tissue hypertrophy, which are not the primary features of the patient's presentation.
